summary:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive aerospace AI-powered web-based dashboard developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge to translate decades of complex microgravity combustion archives into practical space safety guidelines.

What We Developed: An intuitive web platform featuring a 1g versus microgravity flame behavior visualizer, a curated NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) experiment explorer (covering landmark studies like SoFIE and FLEX), and an instant engineering safety assistant.

How It Addresses the Challenge: It bridges the gap between dense academic research and practical application, giving mission planners and engineers an accessible interface to study how reduced-gravity environments alter flame spread, soot production, and extinction limits.

Why It Is Important: Fire in space behaves unpredictably without buoyancy, transforming into silent, spherical diffusion flames that pose extreme risks to spacecraft. As humanity expands toward permanent lunar and Martian habitats, Flame in Freefall equips designers with the critical data needed to build robust, life-saving fire protection systems.
details:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive aerospace dashboard developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

It turns decades of accumulated microgravity combustion data into actionable space safety guidance. It does this by combining a visualiser that compares Earth-based flame behaviour with microgravity flame behaviour, a curated explorer of NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) experiments, and an instant engineering safety assistant.

The assistant is built with React, TypeScript, and Vite. It's all about taking that dense academic data and making it accessible to engineers and future habitat designers in a way that they can actually use it to understand how flames behave in microgravity (how they spread, how much soot they produce, their extinction limits, etc.) and thereby design better fire protection for long-duration spaceflight and for future permanent lunar and Mars bases.

Frontend & Architecture: TypeScript and React powered by Vite.

Styling & UI: Modern responsive CSS/Tailwind with a dark-mode aerospace aesthetic.

Hosting & Deployment: Hosted live via GitHub Pages (xrihab.github.io/flame-in-freefall).

Video & Media Production: macOS tools (iMovie / CapCut) for creating and editing the 30-second submission demonstration video hosted securely via Google Drive.
